## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)). I cannot set labels on this repository; suggested: `orig-external`, `cat-ci`, `area:normalization`, `mod-frost`.

## Affected area

CI or test infrastructure (benchmark only)

## Summary

`benchmark/norms/benchmark_cudnn_vs_frost.py` compares "cuDNN native norm vs cuDNN frost norm". Its `cudnn` worker (`_norm_bench_worker.run_cudnn`) builds the LayerNorm / RMSNorm graphs with the default dispatch.

The FROST norm engines are default candidates on cc 10.0 and 10.3, and on cc 9.0 behind the opt-in. On those parts the "native" leg therefore built `norm_fprop_sm100` / `norm_bprop_sm100`, so the script compared FROST against FROST.

The worker now bars the `frost_norm_fwd` / `frost_norm_bwd` families by name before planning, as `benchmark_single_sdpa.py` does for FROST SDPA on its backend leg. It also prints the plans each graph built (a `PLANS` line), so the leg's route is visible in the output. The `RESULT` line and its parsing are unchanged.

## Why

On SM100 / SM103 the script's speedup column was not a FROST-vs-backend comparison.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

None (benchmark only).

## Testing

B300 SXM6 (cc 10.3), cuDNN 9.27.0.42, develop `af1a5181`, an 8192 x 4096 bf16 graph:

- develop: the `cudnn` worker built `norm_fprop_sm100` and `norm_bprop_sm100`, for both RMSNorm and LayerNorm;
- this change: it builds `eng5_k14=0_k24=0_k33=0_k34=1_k35=0_k36=1_k42=0` (forward) and `eng4_k14=1_k24=2_k30=-1_k33=0_k34=0_k35=2_k36=-1` (backward), both backend plans.

With the fix, `benchmark_cudnn_vs_frost.py` over all 15 model presets on that B300 gives these FROST / backend speedups:

| dtype | forward geomean (range) | backward geomean (range) |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 | 1.03x (0.76-1.24) | 0.98x (0.90-1.09) |
| fp16 | 1.03x (0.76-1.38) | 0.99x (0.76-1.18) |

FROST's correctness check against torch passed in every run. The per-preset table is in the script output.

Reviewed `f822958d4932` against base `11cb888fdb58`.

Thank you for your contribution! No finding. Both norm families are excluded before planning, so the cudnn leg measures the native backend. The selected-plan names agree with the plans that build and execute. The extra PLANS line preserves RESULT parsing; it is visible when invoking the worker directly, while the aggregate driver still captures worker stdout.

Validation: Ran the actual changed cudnn worker on SM100 with cuDNN9.26 for RMSNorm and LayerNorm, FP16 and BF16, at128x256. All four forward/backward runs completed; all eight selected plans were native eng5/eng4 backend plans and none used a barred FROST name. Checked manifest family slots, deselection timing, selected-plan indexing and the aggregate driver's RESULT regex. The actual PLANS output plus RESULT format parsed successfully. Current develop changes do not touch this benchmark or its normalization/planning contracts. Inspected and approved the unchanged fork Style/Security workflows; they have started.

Limitations: The local run checks execution route and parsing, not numerical correctness or performance. Shared GPU load makes its timings unsuitable for comparison; the author's B300 performance claims were not independently reproduced.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

files.patch:
@@ -93,6 +93,22 @@ def run_frost(a):
     return fwd_ms, bwd_ms, fwd_maxabs, bwd_maxabs
 
 
+def _deselect_frost_norm(graph):
+    """The `cudnn` worker measures the native backend. The FROST norm engines are default candidates on the parts they serve
+    (cc 10.0 / 10.3; cc 9.0 behind the opt-in), so bar both families by name and the walk settles on a backend plan, as
+    benchmark_single_sdpa.py does for FROST SDPA on its backend leg."""
+    from cudnn.engines.manifest import MANIFEST
+
+    graph.deselect_engines([name for fam in MANIFEST if fam.name in ("frost_norm_fwd", "frost_norm_bwd") for name in fam.slots])
+
+
+def _plan_name(graph) -> str:
+    try:
+        return graph.get_plan_name_at_index(graph._plan_index)
+    except Exception:
+        return "unknown"
+
+
 def run_cudnn(a):
     import torch
     import cudnn
@@ -124,6 +140,7 @@ def run_cudnn(a):
         MEAN.set_output(True).set_data_type(torch.float32)
     gf.validate()
     gf.build_operation_graph()
+    _deselect_frost_norm(gf)
     gf.create_execution_plans([cudnn.heur_mode.A, cudnn.heur_mode.FALLBACK])
     gf.check_support()
     gf.build_plans()
@@ -158,6 +175,7 @@ def run_cudnn(a):
         DB.set_output(True).set_data_type(dt)
     gb.validate()
     gb.build_operation_graph()
+    _deselect_frost_norm(gb)
     gb.create_execution_plans([cudnn.heur_mode.A, cudnn.heur_mode.FALLBACK])
     gb.check_support()
     gb.build_plans()
@@ -180,6 +198,7 @@ def run_cudnn(a):
 
     fwd_ms = _median_ms(lambda: gf.execute(vpf, ws), a.iters, a.warmup, l2)
     bwd_ms = _median_ms(lambda: gb.execute(vpb, ws), a.iters, a.warmup, l2)
+    print(f"PLANS fwd={_plan_name(gf)} bwd={_plan_name(gb)}")
     return fwd_ms, bwd_ms, -1.0, -1.0  # correctness checked in the frost worker
